output.title: Design against the error loop
output.body:
When a workflow keeps correcting its own mistakes, the problem is usually not the last error. It is the loop that sends bad data back into the same process.

The bounded question I’d ask is simple: which repeated manual task creates the next round of rework? If invoice details are entered by hand and later reconciled by hand because the first entry was incomplete or misclassified, that is the loop to design against. I am not describing a customer result here, just a workflow pattern to look for.

Before you add AI, check whether the workflow is actually a fit. Is it repetitive, does it produce a measurable outcome, and does it already live in digital documents or SaaS tools? If not, AI is probably the wrong tool. Change the process first.

If it does fit, pick one error-blocking control before anything else. Duplicate detection, mandatory field validation, or human approval before a high-risk step are all reasonable design choices. The point is to catch the mistake before it cycles back. Human approval stays mandatory for money movement and other high-risk decisions. Boring, but usually the right kind of boring.

Then scope a pilot around one workflow and one control. Not the whole business. One loop, one gate, one clear place to stop the error from feeding itself.
